evidence: The issue proposes a proactive extension-conflict warning system (declared incompatibilities, install-time and active conflict alerts). None of the candidates describe the same bug; the closest ones are about enabling/disabling extensions, extension source visibility, install target disambiguation, or unrelated AI/chat/UX features.

Both describe changing reasoningEffort for a custom endpoint/model causing the wrong chatLanguageModels.json entry to be overwritten or updated. Candidate #320805 specifically says the setting is applied to the wrong custom endpoint due to index mismatch, matching the overwrite/replace behavior in the issue.

The issue is about double-clicking to select a whole line causing the Ask Questions widget to dismiss. None of the candidates describe this specific interaction; the closest ones involve text selection, focus, or dismissing unrelated UI, but not this same double-click selection bug.

The issue is about Agents window PR detection failing persistently after a repository-scoped GitHub token returns 401. None of the candidates describe the same underlying bug; the closest auth-related one (#320813) is about GitHub sign-in lockout from a missing Authorization header on /user, which is a different failure path and product area.

The issue is about the Help menu missing a 'Report Issue' command / mismatched template text. None of the candidates describe this same UI bug; the closest ones are about issue reporting flows or unrelated chat/permission/reporting problems.

Both describe flickering in the chat input area in the agents/chat panel, and candidate #325589 specifically mentions flickering on resize of the main editor window, which matches a width-dependent flicker in the input region.

Both reports describe the same underlying PowerShell tree-sitter parsing failure that causes terminal auto-approve to fail. The candidate is the direct predecessor reference ('Issue in powershell tree sitter grammar?'), and the main issue explicitly says it follows from #294010 and discusses the same parse bugs (`--` separator, `./path`, and related masking/workarounds).

The issue is a specific flaky unit test in CopilotAgent resumeSession logic timing out after a Start Over truncate leaves the session empty. None of the candidates describe this same test or the same fallback-after-truncate bug; they cover unrelated smoke tests, session loss, crashes, hangs, auth/status refresh, or generic flakiness.

The issue is about a null dereference in IndentGuidesOverlay.prepareRender when visibleRangeForPosition returns null. None of the candidates mention indent guides, visible range, or this rendering null-check bug; they are about unrelated cursor prediction, MultiDiffEditorWidget disposal, gitRepository state, chat model picker, scrollbar styling, testing output, quick diff, documents, or accessibility.
All candidates and the issue have the exact same title and body snippet ('Copilot completion feedback' / same template), indicating the same underlying report.

The issue is too vague and only mentions a pyright undefined-variable ignore comment; none of the candidates clearly describe the same specific bug. The closest undefined-variable report (#320588) is about VS Code failing to detect an undefined variable in local problems, but the given issue lacks enough detail to confirm it is the same underlying bug.

The issue is about intermittent mocha timeouts in specific AgentHost node I/O tests on Windows CI, fixed by increasing test timeouts. None of the candidates describe the same underlying bug; they cover hangs, feature work, networking behavior, smoke test failures, or unrelated issues.

Both describe Copilot Chat discovery scanning the whole workspace with `rg --no-ignore --follow`, causing repeated high-CPU/ripgrep storms. Candidate #323094 specifically covers the same AGENTS.md discovery path and same flags/pathology as the reported chat customization discovery loop.

The issue is about missing padding between the remote indicator and the restricted mode indicator. None of the candidates specifically mention these two indicators or the same UI spacing bug; the closest ones are about unrelated padding, tabs, terminal, or sidebar/icon spacing.

The issue is about Code.exe launching differently from code.cmd on Windows, likely due to environment/shortcut/launcher differences and extensions not loading. None of the candidates describe this same startup path-specific bug; they cover unrelated terminal, WSL/profile, dialog freezing, right-click context menu, debugging, or junction issues.

The issue text is too unclear/garbled to identify a specific bug. None of the candidates clearly describe the same underlying problem; at best they are generic 'not working' or unrelated UI/loading complaints.

Candidate #321565 is about a PR failed CI icon and specifically requests a PR icon with a failure indication. The issue here also concerns the failed CI icon being confusing, hard to read, and having bad contrast, which matches the same underlying UI/icon problem.

Both reports are about the integrated terminal/window being unavailable in the CS50 Codespaces/VS Code environment. Candidate #313570 specifically says the terminal window cannot be opened and closes immediately, which matches the core terminal-not-working symptom better than the other candidates.

The candidate issues are mostly about other overflow/clipping problems (tabs, scrollbar, popup, title overlap, buttons in other views) and do not describe the same terminal panel close-button overflow bug. The closest ones involve tab close buttons being hidden by tab actions, but those are editor tab issues, not the terminal panel close button in Modern UI.

Candidate #323294 is explicitly the same McpStdioStateHandler flake, describing "McpStdioStateHandler sigterm after grace" with retries passing. The other candidates are different MCP/terminal/chat or unrelated flakiness issues.

The issue is about XML/markup injection in workspace skill descriptions corrupting the customizations index and affecting ReadFile confirmation for external URIs. None of the candidates describe this underlying bug; they cover unrelated tool hangs, workspace trust/model picker behavior, UI rendering, prompt caching, file context duplication, discovery settings, sandboxing, indexing auth, and slash command availability.

The issue is about lack of visual hierarchy/nesting between a session and its subsessions in the sessions view. None of the candidates describe this same underlying bug; most are about ordering, duplicates, icons, worktree selection, or separate session list behaviors rather than subsession hierarchy.

The issue is specifically about periodic host-owned refresh of agent host model catalogs and preserving stale data across long-lived sessions. The candidates mostly concern different model-picker, auth, or provider-specific failures (missing models, 429s, BYOK, GHE auth, session UI bugs) rather than the same periodic refresh bug.

The issue is about `/btw` not indicating that a message has other attached context. None of the candidates describe this specific UX/attachment indicator problem; the closest ones are about context sizing, attachment behavior, or unrelated rendering/debug bugs.

The issue is about incorrect caret/selection rendering inside a wrapped Markdown table cell in the Agents window. None of the candidates describe this specific visual-caret bug; the closest Markdown editor/table issues are about performance or rendering/layout settings, not a multi-line caret in wrapped cells.

The issue only says SSH to 172.17.12.121 could not be established and VS Code Server failed to install, but gives no specific failure mode (404, timeout, socket limit, wrong version, etc.). None of the candidates match this exact underlying bug with enough certainty.
Same error string and same Copilot chat prompting flow; candidate #323182 explicitly says opening Copilot Chat and typing a prompt yields 'Language Model Unavailable'.

The issue is about the @ symbol/file tagging suggestions failing in a WSL workspace. None of the candidates describe workspace-file @ tagging or suggestion dropdown behavior in WSL; most are about copy/paste, search, terminal links, Git, or unrelated features.

Candidate #323478 says in Portuguese that the project was deleted and asks how to recover it, which matches the same underlying bug: agent destroyed/deleted the user's project and it cannot be restored.

The issue is specifically about Autopilot treating a non-empty text-only assistant response as completion instead of continuing until task_complete is called. Most candidates are about different failures (stuck thinking, missing rendering, command approval, terminal output, handoffs, or UI mode mismatches). Candidate #320313 discusses Advanced Autopilot/evaluator logic and #321054/#285063 are vaguely about stopping early, but neither clearly matches the exact text-only-response-without-task_complete bug.

The issue describes confusing interaction/usability of the comment bubble, while the candidates are about unrelated bugs like focus, tooltips, layout, scrolling, clipping, errors, or flicker. None matches a specific underlying comment-bubble interaction bug.

The issue is about invalid Kimi-generated tool_use.id values containing dots/colons causing Anthropic 400s on later replayed requests. None of the candidates describe this same ID-format sanitation/replay problem; the closest Kimi-related candidates concern temperature handling or output parsing, not malformed tool_use IDs.

The issue is about inline completions ignoring the preferred/selected language after changing a file from .rs to JavaScript. None of the candidates describe this same bug; the closest ones are unrelated Copilot availability/model errors or empty/garbled titles.

The issue is about duplicate MCP server definitions appearing in the UI due to multiple plugins contributing the same servers. None of the candidates describe duplicate server definitions from plugins; they cover tool name collisions, authentication/startup failures, disappearing servers, or discovery bugs.

The report is about agents freezing, looping, creating new folders/copies, wasting budget, and not producing results. The candidates cover nearby but distinct problems: budget/quota handling, disabled tools after budget restores, patch/apply hangs, terminal/session destruction, cache misses, or generic credit waste. None clearly matches the specific underlying bug of agents going in circles and spawning extra folders/copies while burning budget.

The issue is about deferring a chat list height update to the next animation frame (fixes #316501). None of the candidates describe this underlying bug; they are about unrelated cursor prediction, git repository access, multi-diff widget disposal, auth-change deduping, agent host session state, file-write redirection, UI spacing, or test/workflow changes.

The report is about Claude Code for VS Code leaking memory while idle in Linux until system OOM kill. None of the candidates clearly describe the same idle Claude Code memory leak on Linux; the closest ones involve different products (Copilot/ChatGPT/Codex), different triggers (chat opening, agent sessions, terminal tool use, remote SSH), or only generic high CPU/memory issues.

Issue #327582 is a tracker issue listing UX research insights and specific sub-issues for the chats system model. Candidate #322934 is the underlying research/design issue about making the session/chat relationship visible through UI structure, and its listed directions include the same nested-chats and onboarding ideas referenced in #327582.

The issue is about consolidating multiple browser element attachments into a single visible attachment per element (text + optional screenshot). None of the candidates describe this specific UI grouping bug; the closest ones are about element/chat context, screenshots rendering, or attachment handling, but not combining multiple element attachments into one item.

The issue is about missing command 'workbench.action.chat.openPlan' in chat tip action handling. None of the candidates describe that same missing-command bug; the closest chat-related ones are different failures (workspace resolution, invalid JSON, network/server errors, undefined property, response stream closed, etc.).

The issue is about the GitHub authentication extension making an unnecessary education.github.com telemetry request on each window launch, especially for EMU accounts. None of the candidates describe that same education.github.com call or this telemetry/EMU behavior; they cover unrelated auth, telemetry, Copilot, chat, marketplace, or git issues.

The issue text is only a placeholder ('Control' with empty numbered steps) and the candidates are likewise non-descriptive placeholders. There is no substantive bug detail to establish a duplicate underlying issue.

The report is about VS Code opening like a first-time install with all projects/workspaces gone, which suggests lost state or missing recent items. None of the candidates clearly describe the same underlying bug; most are about explorer/UI hiding, session restoration, crashes, or unrelated file deletion.

Both discuss the Agents window new-session/detail panel showing the Changes view for a new session. Candidate #324566 explicitly asks whether a new session screen should also show a Changes section, matching the same underlying behavior as ISSUE #327526.

The issue is about settings JSON validation/intellisense failing for nested `workbench.colorCustomizations` theme-scoped properties while colors still apply. None of the candidates describe this same underlying bug; they are about theme contrast, wrong colors, sidebar/menu behavior, or unrelated UI issues.

The issue is about a specific BYOK Anthropic model being misconfigured with wrong context window and vision support. None of the candidates describe the same model metadata/vision capability bug; most are about missing models, selection persistence, agent window differences, or unrelated 400/thinking errors.

Both reports describe code-server/serve-web where switching the display language to Chinese causes the translation/localization to break. Candidate #323289 specifically says 'Code Server Display Language Broken' and reproduces with `code serve-web` then switching to Chinese, matching the same underlying bug.

The issue is about a setting not persisting across VS Code profiles and suggesting it should be machine-level/cross-profile. None of the candidates describe the same broker-implementation setting; the closest ones are about profile-scoped defaults or unrelated settings/model/session persistence, not this specific bug.

Both describe feedback on changed files/agent changes where submitting feedback appears to do nothing / lacks UI response. Candidate #313319 explicitly says changed-file feedback cannot be successfully submitted and there is no UI/UX response, matching the reported broken Submit button while feedback is queued.

The issue is a specific crash caused by `ModelList.validator` allowing a missing `models` field, leading to `.filter` on `undefined`. None of the candidates describe this same validator/`models`-missing crash; they cover unrelated model picker, configuration, token counting, rate-limit, or other Copilot bugs.
Both issue titles are essentially the same placeholder text: 'det' vs 'what', and both descriptions are the identical template asking to describe expected outcome and attach a screenshot.

The issue text is just a placeholder name ('Rathana') followed by the generic prompt 'Please describe the expected outcome and attach a screenshot!'. None of the candidates provide matching underlying bug details beyond similarly incomplete placeholder text, so a true canonical cannot be established.

Both report Codespaces getting stuck while connecting/loading, with the editor/terminal not becoming usable. Candidate #324428 specifically says it stalls at "Setting up remote connection" and never reaches editor or terminal, which matches the described unusable Codespace state.

The issue is a generic null dereference reading 'name'. None of the candidates point to the same underlying bug; they involve different properties ('undefined', 'node', 'id', 'metadata', etc.) and different stack locations, so there is no clear canonical match.

Both report a Codespaces workspace failing to open / set up the connection, with the editor not coming up. Candidate #324302 specifically says the code space is not opening and GitHub cannot set up the connection, matching the generic 'not working' report.

The notes mention specific Voice Mode UI feedback about placeholder text flashing in purple speaking mode, subtler glow states, and double-button sizing. Candidate #322158 is the only Voice Mode issue and explicitly covers the purple speaking state and voice-mode UI behavior, making it the closest canonical match.

The issue is about Copilot/chat showing "Language model unavailable" and not working; candidate #322132 describes the same exact error while using chat. Several others are near-identical, but #322132 is the closest canonical match.

The reported bug is about Microsoft Pinyin IME composition leaving a file marked dirty even though text content is unchanged. The candidates are about unrelated save failures, crashes, duplicate/restore issues, or general IME input problems; none describe the same ‘unchanged but unsaved/dirty after canceled IME input’ behavior.

The issue is about the experimental Markdown editor keeping an empty paragraph as transient view state until navigation cancels it. None of the candidates describe this same underlying bug; they cover preview toggles, corruption, clipboard, IME input, scroll restoration, file association, Mermaid rendering, or other unrelated Markdown/editor problems.

Both describe the same PR review/commenting UI problem in GitHub Pull Requests: the plus button used to add an inline comment is not working/active. Candidate #323682 specifically reports clicking '+' to add comment not focusing the feedback input box.

The issue is about caret navigation in the experimental Markdown editor where Home/End jump to paragraph boundaries instead of wrapped visual-line boundaries. None of the candidates describe the same bug; they cover test result rendering, diff word wrap, preview parsing/highlighting, terminal/UI clipping, keyboard shortcuts, IME input, or other Agents window/editor layout problems.

Both describe the new subagent UX in the Agents window: inline pill/spinner/progress for running subagents and opening a subagent into a side/multi-chat. Candidate #324362 explicitly covers read-only subagent chats, the running subagents chip, and the inline 'Open Subagent' pill.

The issue is about Markdown comment UI polish (consistent size/shape/position across states, removing 'You', matching shadows/radii/colors). None of the candidates describe this same Markdown comment/comment composer bug; they cover unrelated UI modernization items like icons, scrollbars, panels, terminal padding, or editor tabs.

The issue asks for GitHub Copilot Desktop APP support for devcontainer integration, while the candidates mostly concern unrelated devcontainer UX, remote lifecycle, or terminal/agent sandboxing bugs. Candidate #282778 is about Copilot Chat in VS Code for Web, but not the same underlying bug or feature request.

The issue is about a dashboard chart/employee utilization bar being continuous across weekends/holidays when adjacent days are red. None of the candidates describe this specific time-series visualization bug; they are about agents UI, placeholders, terminal titles, credits, or unrelated settings.

The issue is about Generate Commit Message failing with HTTP 422 and promptFiltered on free_educational_quota/gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18. The closest candidates (#322788, #322838, #322817, #321184) are about 400 model_not_supported or model resolution failures, not the same 422 backend rejection, and the others are unrelated.

The issue is about restoring web_fetch access to private/local networks or allowlisting DNSs for internal sites. None of the candidates describe web_fetch/private network blocking; the closest networking/auth issues are unrelated (retries, proxying, auth, sandbox, terminal approval).

Both request a standardized ignore file for AI tools: the issue proposes standardizing .noai/.aiignore and supporting these files, while candidate #320821 asks for a .aiignore file to exclude files from AI agents.

The issue is specifically about reducing vertical space in the status bar. None of the candidates mention the status bar; they cover welcome pages, sidebar/activity bar compactness, terminal/panel padding, or unrelated UI spacing/icon issues. No same underlying bug is evident.

The issue is about introducing/showing a Changes view when starting a new session. The candidates are mostly about related but different problems: whether the Changes tab should appear when there are no changes, diff editor actions, layout/persistence bugs, or study feedback. None clearly describe the same underlying bug of missing a Changes view for a new session.

The issue is about moving ExP to the fetcher service as part of ExP client migration to a GH-hosted ExP service. None of the candidates describe this specific migration or fetcher-service move; they cover unrelated agent host, auth, UI, networking, or session issues.

The report is about Copilot unexpectedly defaulting to Auto model selection and using plan credits during chats. None of the candidates describe the same bug: several are about different auto/model persistence scenarios, plan/agent mode behavior, credit warnings, or model availability, but not this specific issue of always routing to Auto despite default model settings and draining credits.

Both describe the same underlying bug: one request/session materializing into two identical cloud/agent sessions in the Agents window. Candidate 13 explicitly says two identical sessions are triggered from one request, matching the duplicate cloud sessions reported here.

The issue is about hidden chat transcripts still being treated as visible, causing dynamic-height rows to measure 0px and emit warnings under display:none. None of the candidates describe this visibility/lifecycle bug; they cover unrelated problems like stuck running status, new chat failures, model selection sharing, empty transcripts, hidden items in lists, or layout pane selection.

The issue is about Agent Host MCP auto-auth reporting a false failure after a successful authentication handoff due to a duplicate probe / missing pending consumer. None of the candidates describe this same underlying bug; nearby MCP auth issues concern stale tokens, XAA, Entra resource/scope conflicts, or unrelated session/UI behavior.

The issue is about losing persisted dynamic OAuth/MCP auth state after an extension-host restart, causing repeated Authenticate prompts for a remote MCP server. None of the candidates describe this same underlying bug; the closest (#321834) is about stale tokens/client eviction on 401 without restart, while others concern different auth flows, session lifecycle, or unrelated MCP/tool issues.
Both describe GitHub Copilot chat suddenly returning 'Language model unavailable' across agents/models, and candidate #322132 is the same generic error report.

The issue is about standard VS Code startup failing specifically because Git does not load and login is blocked, with a workaround via `--disable-extensions` or a fresh user data dir. None of the candidates describe this same underlying startup/Git-loading bug; most are about Copilot/chat sign-in, auth loops, terminal hangs, or unrelated extension host/marketplace issues.

Candidate #320568 explicitly reports GitHub Copilot/Chat not working with WSL and extension incompatibility on WSL2. The issue text says the GitHub Copilot Desktop App does not support WSL integration, which is the same underlying bug.

Both reports describe an agent session where tools are enabled in configuration but the first/previous successful prompt is followed by a later prompt that has no tools or treats them as disabled. Candidate #321882 specifically says chats created from the Agents window on Local sessions don't get tools in their first message, which is the closest match to the same underlying tool-availability bug.

The issue is a feature request for smarter untitled-file Save As name suggestion by scanning top comment lines and stripping comment markers. None of the candidates describe this bug/feature; the closest terminal/snippet/file-picker items are unrelated.
Both reports describe GitHub Copilot Chat failing/stalling during activation in VS Code, with the extension showing as 'activating' and Copilot unusable.

Both describe Remote-SSH/remote session disconnect behavior where the remote server/container/CLI continues running after VS Code disconnects or the connection is closed. Candidate #321118 specifically says Dev Containers remain running after closing VS Code or using Close Remote Connection, matching the underlying lifecycle bug.

The issue is about VS Code reading the user-level MCP config from ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json so CLI-managed servers appear in VS Code. None of the candidates discuss this config-file interoperability; they are about plugin cwd/env vars, remote workspace path issues, naming collisions, origin tracing, settings/MDM, OAuth, or tool scoping.

The issue requests adding Save/Save As actions to the tab right-click menu. The candidates are about compare-with-saved, opening items in new windows, moving terminals/panels, tab closing/layout bugs, or other unrelated features, not the same underlying bug/feature request.

The issue is about the Issue Reporter allowing users to attach their own screenshots/videos from clipboard or drag-and-drop. None of the candidates describe that same bug; the closest ones are about taking screenshots in the agents window or other chat/attachment problems, not attaching media into the issue reporter from clipboard/drag and drop.

The issue is a complaint about a specific VS Code Marketplace AI extension (BlackboxAI) being unreliable, nonresponsive support, and possibly scam-like billing/marketing. None of the candidates describe the same underlying bug; most are about Copilot/AI suggestion behavior, authentication, marketplace access, billing, or unrelated features.

The report describes startup/restart failure with account sign-out, extensions not working, update/install hangs, and reinstall hanging. None of the candidates clearly match this same underlying bug; most are about extension host crashes, login loops, terminal issues, or extension install failures in different contexts. The closest login-related ones still do not match the broader launch/install hang behavior.

The issue is about a Linux integrated terminal launch failure caused by a specific libnode.so version mismatch/hard-coded dependency. None of the candidates describe the same underlying bug; most are about terminal environment warnings, shell integration behavior, rendering, Windows conpty, or unrelated extension/CLI problems.

Both reports are about a GitHub MCP app failing during/after reload. The candidate specifically mentions a timed-out GitHub auth provider registration, which fits the described reload session error more closely than the other generic/error-only candidates.

The issue is about Tab key behavior inside the Agents window Markdown editor moving focus to the Editing/Locked toggle instead of indenting a list item. None of the candidates describe this same underlying bug; the closest ones are generic focus/tab-order or Markdown preview shortcut issues, but not this specific editor focus regression.

Candidate #324879 describes the same underlying behavior in the integrated browser: when a tooltip is shown, the browser unexpectedly scales/shifts and is dimmed, then returns to normal when the tooltip disappears. The issue here also reports browser content dimming only when a tooltip or control overlaps the browser area.

The issue is about missing/incorrect OpenTelemetry emission of chat session titles and session ID joinability, not about chat UI title generation, renaming, rendering, or session list/filter presentation. None of the candidates describe the same telemetry/OTel attribute bug.

Both issues describe the same underlying PowerShell parsing mismatch in terminal auto-approval: the command auto-approver is using the wrong grammar / parsing PowerShell commands incorrectly, causing rules to miss or re-prompt. Candidate #294010 explicitly says "PowerShell auto approve incorrectly parsing command" and points to the PowerShell tree-sitter grammar, matching the bug described here.

None of the candidates describe the Markdown editor selection bug where Cmd+A appears to select all but typing inserts into a pending paragraph instead of replacing it. Related Markdown/preview issues and unrelated editor/webview bugs do not match the same underlying behavior.

The issue is about a missing 'No' option when VS Code prompts to open a detected Git repository. None of the candidates describe this specific prompt; they concern worktree UI, trust dialogs, confirmations for other actions, or unrelated Git features.
Candidate #325645 says essentially the same thing: "i cant turn it off" under Copilot completion feedback, matching the user's request to disable a feature.

The issue asks to add OpenCode to the AHP harness list and ensure it works with DevContainers/remote development. None of the candidates are about OpenCode; the closest ones discuss Claude/Codex/Multi-Chat, tool support, UI, or unrelated AHP bugs.

Both describe Agent Host/system notifications that need to persist and be visible across session lifecycle/sessions. The candidate explicitly covers preserving and rendering system notifications across restored sessions and during live turns, which matches the user’s concern about notifications across sessions.

The issue is about increasing vertical spacing between Activity Bar buttons in Modern UI default size. None of the candidates describe that same default-size vertical spacing bug; the closest are compact-mode or badge/contrast/layout issues, but they concern different modes or different UI elements.

The issue is a terminal renderer crash/stall in an auxiliary window caused by U+2591/U+2592/U+2593 triggering drawPatternChar and createElement throwing in a child window. None of the candidates describe this specific shade-character / custom glyph rasterizer / auxiliary-window failure mode; they cover unrelated font rendering, GPU atlas corruption, shell integration, crashes, or Copilot/tool issues.

The issue is a vague inability to upgrade a GitHub plan and says GitHub is 'acting up,' but the candidates are mostly specific Copilot/chat/request-limit or sign-in problems. Candidate #320737 is closest ('Unable to upgrade copilot pro') yet the underlying bug is not identifiable as the same from the given content, so no true canonical can be confirmed.

The issue asks for a dashboard widget showing project hours grouped by project, with planned vs assigned hours and per-employee breakdown. None of the candidates describe project-hour reporting or workload visualization; the closest ones are about tokens, session changes, or Agents UI layout, which are unrelated.

The issue is simply "Unable to update" / cannot update VS Code, which matches the generic update-failure report in candidate #325048 ('Cannot update'). The other candidates are either more specific update scenarios or unrelated.

The issue is about Marketplace manifest deprecation and migration from one VS Code extension publisher to another. None of the candidates discuss deprecating `dotutils.binlog-analyzer` or an extension Marketplace deprecation banner/migrate flow for this extension; the closest deprecation-related candidates concern unrelated features (Copilot terminal content, Ollama provider, chat mode, review, etc.).

Both describe runtime slash commands (notably /chronicle) missing from autocomplete until after a first message/session creation. Candidate #324645 explicitly states runtime slash commands do not autocomplete in the new-session composer before the session exists, then appear after the first message.

Both describe a file contents refresh/persistence problem where the file appears empty or not updated in the editor/UI even though the data exists on disk. Candidate #321365 specifically reports files becoming empty after reopening, matching the underlying bug more closely than the other candidates.

The issue is specifically about adding a new `rename_session` tool/API to Agent Host session-management tools so agents can rename sessions directly. The candidates are mostly about UI renaming in chat/Agents windows, persistence bugs, session grouping, or unrelated session-management features, and none clearly describe the same underlying API addition.

The issue is about environment variables from the first VS Code window/main process carrying over into later windows. None of the candidates describe cross-window environment inheritance on startup; the closest terminal environment issues are about extension-contributed terminal env, restart warnings, or terminal popup UI, not shared main-process env leakage across windows.

The issue is about @agentPlugins failing to discover plugins from user-configured chat.plugins.marketplaces after the 1.131 agent host rearchitecture. None of the candidates describe that same discovery/filtering regression; they involve uninstall persistence, install-from-source UI, marketplace versioning, agent dropdown/session restoration, or unrelated model/tool issues.

Both describe Copilot quota/credit limit exhaustion causing a persistent UI issue after the limit is reached. Candidate #322110 is the closest canonical because it explicitly reports the monthly credit limit being reached and mentions the same language model access path; the flashing status in the issue appears to be the user-facing indicator of that limit state.

The issue is about compile-time drift in AHP listSessions mappers silently dropping optional wire fields between producer/consumer object mappers. None of the candidates describe this underlying bug; they cover unrelated session UI/state, performance, telemetry, architecture, or test issues.

Candidates are about unrelated terminal problems (Ctrl+C handling in fish, clipboard OSC 52 decoding, silent shell execution streams, cursor position, restart warnings, input/rendering, keybinding conflicts, font overlap, multiline corruption, etc.). None describe the same BEL/OSC 633 terminator causing a bell on every prompt.

None of the candidates describe this specific speech-to-text irreversibility bug; the closest voice-mode candidates are about push-to-talk behavior, model selection, or session state, which are different underlying issues.

Candidate #324078 mentions the Modern UI and a menu-related visual issue where the highlight/focus indicator is very light and hard to see; the reported problem is likewise that the top menu bar in the new Modern UI does not follow dark theme colors (black font on dark theme).

The issue text is too garbled/general to identify a specific underlying bug. None of the candidates clearly describe the same problem; at best a few mention generic loading or showing problems, but not the same actionable issue.

None of the candidates describe queued custom commands being combined; the closest /compact or model-selection bugs are about compaction model choice, thinking effort persistence, utility model routing, or retry/model mismatch, which are different underlying bugs.

None of the candidates describe this same title-update-driven UI lockup; they cover unrelated terminal restart warnings, overlap/clipping, Copilot listener leaks, task rerun behavior, command output truncation, freezes on paste, or other agent/session problems.

The issue is about adding telemetry for Claude Code conversation messages and chat titles. None of the candidates discuss telemetry or emitting conversation/title events; they cover multi-chat UI, prompts, auth, debug logs, branding, slash commands, or unrelated Claude/Copilot bugs.
Both describe a Codespaces startup/connect failure that stalls at remote connection/setup and never reaches the editor or terminal.

The issue is about `npm run hygiene` producing many hygiene warnings/errors and cluttering output. None of the candidates describe the same underlying bug; they are about unrelated diagnostics, logging, UI glitches, or specific language-feature false positives rather than hygiene report generation or filtering.

The issue text is too vague ('i dont now' / 'pls help, no selection model llm') and does not clearly describe the same underlying bug as any candidate. Several candidates mention model selection or unavailable models, but there is insufficient detail to match a specific canonical.

The issue is about missing user-facing notification when an MCP server cannot access the selected model permission. None of the candidates describe this model-access permission discoverability bug; they instead cover OAuth/DCR/auth token handling, tool discovery, model picker visibility, or unrelated MCP errors.

The issue is about deferring a chat list height update to the next animation frame, while all candidates are about unrelated bugs (cursor prediction, gitRepository null access, MultiDiffEditorWidget disposal, ADO auth-change re-fetching, etc.) and do not describe the same underlying bug.

Both describe a slash-command-related failure in Claude/Agent Host where entering a command in the chat input does not work and instead triggers an error or blocked send. Candidate #323728 specifically says slash commands like `/code-review` are blocked in Claude Agent SDK chat input; this matches the underlying bug more closely than the other multi-chat/focus issues.
